title: PyTorch Stable Documentation
summary: The current stable documentation index organizes installation, the user guide, reference APIs, developer notes, and advanced topics such as compilation and export. Stable APIs aim for backward compatibility; experimental APIs may evolve.

title: Extending PyTorch
summary: Official guidance for extending torch.nn, torch.autograd, and native operator dispatch. Custom backward logic should be validated with gradcheck; operator work may require dispatch, autograd, and transform support.

title: torch.distributed
summary: The distributed package provides process groups and communication primitives such as all-reduce, broadcast, gather, and scatter, with backend and device considerations for multi-process and multi-node training.

title: torch.func
summary: Composable transformations such as grad, vmap, jacrev, and jacfwd support per-sample gradients, batched function evaluation, and differentiable programming workflows. Check each transform's compatibility contract.

title: torch.compiler
summary: torch.compile captures and optimizes supported workloads through compiler components including TorchDynamo, AOT Autograd, and TorchInductor. Graph breaks, recompilation, backend support, and warmup affect speedups.

title: torch.export
summary: torch.export captures a module into an exported program with graph constraints and supports serialization for ahead-of-time workflows. Its graph-capture contract differs from torch.compile's eager fallback behavior.

title: Performance Tuning Guide
summary: Performance guidance includes input-pipeline tuning, avoiding unnecessary autograd work, fusion, memory formats, mixed precision, Tensor Core usage, CUDA graphs, and distributed training. Measure before applying optimizations.

title: Quantization
summary: The quantization documentation describes a transition of quantization development toward torchao and provides migration pointers for older eager, FX, and PT2E workflows. New projects should check the current supported recipes.

title: torch.onnx
summary: torch.onnx exports models to the ONNX graph format for interoperable runtimes. Exporter behavior and supported operators vary by PyTorch version, opset, and target runtime, so output parity and deployment tests are essential.

title: torch.profiler
summary: The profiler collects operator timing, memory and trace information for CPU and supported accelerators. Profiling schedules can separate warmup and active windows to limit trace overhead.

title: Tensor Views
summary: View operations share underlying storage when possible. Strides and layout determine whether view is valid; reshape can return either a view or a copy. Aliasing matters for in-place mutation and performance.

title: Reproducibility
summary: Seeds help reproduce random streams but do not guarantee universal bitwise equality across versions, hardware, or kernels. Deterministic-algorithm options, worker seeds, backend settings, and saved RNG state may all matter.

title: DataLoader
summary: Data loading APIs distinguish map-style and iterable datasets and expose batching, samplers, worker processes, prefetching, pinning, and custom collation. Multi-worker and distributed data sharding require attention to duplicate samples.

title: torch.nn.Module
summary: Modules register submodules, parameters and buffers, support train/eval modes, and provide state dictionaries. Correct registration is essential for optimizer discovery, checkpointing, and device movement.
